podcast.title: College and Jobs
podcast.body: Colin secured a coveted spot at Cambridge University, where he pursued studies in English literature. During his pre-Radiohead years, he worked at two local record stores: Manic Hedgehog and Our Price. At these stores, he proactively distributed "On a Friday" demos to visiting record company representatives. He also held a position as the school's entertainment director. "Colin landed a hard-to-get-spotted Cambridge where he studied English literature."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Life and Music
podcast.body: Colin, along with his younger brother Johnny, became involved in music during their early teenage years. Their interest was significantly influenced by an older sister who was keen on bands such as George Evasion in the Fall. "Thanks to an older sister who was in debates like George Evasion in the Fall, the two brothers Colin and Johnny Greenwood got into music together in their early teens."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Origin
podcast.body: Colin Greenwood is originally from Oxford, England. "He's from Oxford."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Band Formation (1982)
xref.body: The core members, Tom York, Colin Greenwood, and Ed O'Brien, first met and started playing together in their final year at Abingdon, a private school in Oxford, around 1982. At this time, they were approximately 14 or 15 years old. Their initial setup included "three guitarists and a bad drum machine named Dr. Rhythm," and their very first gig was at a friend's birthday party. "Their first gig was at a friends birthday party. This would be sometime in 1982, which means everybody was about 14, 15 years old at the time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Hiatus for College (1991)
xref.body: In 1991, "On a Friday" entered an extended hiatus as all five members pursued higher education at different universities. Ed O'Brien went to Manchester University, Colin Greenwood studied English literature at Cambridge, Phil Selway also studied English literature at Liverpool University, and Johnny Greenwood enrolled in both music and psychology programs at Oxford. Tom York decided to take a year off before attending university. "In 1997, a 1991 on a Friday went on an extended sort of hiatus."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Manic Hedgehog Tape (1991)
xref.body: This was a five-song cassette that "On a Friday" sold for three pounds at the local indie record store, Manic Hedgehog, where Colin Greenwood worked. Colin strategically "slipped a copy of this cassette" to any record label representatives who visited the store. This grassroots promotion led to an unprecedented 25 record company reps attending their pivotal gig at the Jericho Tavern. "That cassette ended up being referred to as appropriately the Manic Hedgehog tape and it featured songs like this. It's called Philip a Chicken."

xref.title: Early Lineup with Saxophone
xref.body: The 1986 4-track cassette lineup of On a Friday included a saxophone player, and Jonny Greenwood had not yet joined the band. "At the time, Anna Friday had a saxophone player and did not yet include Colin Greenwood's younger brother Johnny."

xref.title: Saxophone Player in Early Lineup
xref.body: In 1986, when the band was still known as On a Friday and recorded their first 4-track cassette, their lineup included a saxophone player, and Jonny Greenwood had not yet joined. "At the time, Anna Friday had a saxophone player and did not yet include Colin Greenwood's younger brother Johnny."
